solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Duke advanced at great cost

parts.note: advanced in time, as in an advanced hour, means early

explanation.surface: A duke moved ahead in the world, paying heavily for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying dearly means paying a high price, so the adverb matches 'at great cost'.

clue.text: A tie is dated? That's hard to swallow!

parts.note: something out of date or obsolete is dead
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to swallow food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone scorns an old-fashioned necktie as an incredible claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' and 'to' are link words; the pieces run in order: dated, hard, swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race, a finish where two competitors cannot be separated is a tie.

clue.text: Dislike adult adaptation

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
an adaptation of a book or play is a new version of it

explanation.surface: Someone hates a grown-up rewrite of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Instrument left with Victorian pick-up

parts.note: a ute is the Australian word for a pick-up truck, and Victoria is an Australian state

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is abandoned beside a nineteenth-century gramophone pick-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' suggests the 1800s; here it means from the Australian state, where a pick-up truck is a ute.
explanation.definitionFit: The lute is a plucked stringed instrument with a rounded body, popular in Renaissance music.

clue.text: Instrument included in mail for the front line

indicators.note: one word being included in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: to mail a letter is to send it
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is packed into a parcel for soldiers at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharp end is an idiom for where the real action or danger is, such as the front line.

clue.text: Analyst leads woman round bowling area

parts.note: those who lead a group are its heads

indicators.note: the word for a woman goes round, surrounding the bowling area

parts.note: her is a pronoun referring to a woman
a rink is a strip of a bowling green where one game is played

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist takes a woman around the bowling green.
explanation.walkthrough: In the game of bowls, a rink is one strip of the green where a single match is played; 'round' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Headshrinker is a slang term for a psychiatrist or psychoanalyst, someone who analyses minds.

clue.text: Daily grind's hard for girl

parts.note: a dull routine you cannot escape is a rut
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A girl finds the daily routine tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a girl's first name, the kind of example crosswords use for 'girl'.

clue.text: Amorous man conceals books

indicators.note: the man's name hides the books inside itself

parts.note: Eric is a man's name
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A lover hides some books, perhaps of a racy kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic means arousing or concerned with sexual desire, close to amorous.

clue.text: Setting out in drag shows bravery

indicators.note: setting out letters means arranging them afresh, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Going out dressed in women's clothes takes courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting out' signals rearranging the six letters of IN DRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring as a noun is boldness or courage, a synonym of bravery.

clue.text: A convenience for intermediaries

parts.note: a convenience is a public toilet, and a gents is a men's toilet

explanation.surface: A toilet is offered to middlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a 'convenience' is a public lavatory, and the gents is the men's one.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents act on behalf of others, standing between parties as go-betweens.

clue.text: Launch has reversing space in Devon

parts.note: to launch something through the air is to dart or throw it

indicators.note: the word for space is read backwards

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A boat launch has space for turning around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launch' reads as a boat but means throw, DART; ROOM read backwards gives MOOR. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmoor is a large upland national park located in the county of Devon.

clue.text: Part in 7 play for skilled operator

indicators.note: play suggests loose or free movement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer to 7 down, which means amorous

explanation.surface: A role in a racy play goes to an expert performer.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' stands for the answer to 7 down; its letters join PART IN and 'play' shuffles all twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner is someone actively engaged in a skilled profession, such as medicine or law.

clue.text: Weed round first of seedlings and water

indicators.note: the garden tool word goes round the single letter

parts.note: to weed a bed is to hoe it

indicators.note: only the opening letter of seedlings is used

explanation.surface: A gardener weeds around young plants and waters them.
explanation.definitionFit: To hose a garden is to spray water on it, so the verb means to water.

clue.text: German has file to keep hold of

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file for shaping wood or metal

explanation.surface: A German holds on tight to a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp is to grip firmly, which is to keep hold of something.

clue.text: People adopting independent bearing

indicators.note: the word for people takes in the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: men can mean people in general

explanation.surface: People take on an air of self-reliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or manner, the way they carry themselves.

clue.text: Deceive bird touring Spain

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the bird surrounds the letter

parts.note: the chat is a small songbird such as the stonechat
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A migrating bird travelling round Spain fools someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat is to trick or defraud, the same as to deceive.

clue.text: Answer is to have money in bank

indicators.note: the money is placed inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
P stands for pence, a unit of money

explanation.surface: The response is to keep your cash in the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is the verb, as in bank on, meaning rely.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply is a response given to a question, the same as an answer.

clue.text: Old chemists' hop tea treated dental problem

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: caries is tooth decay

explanation.surface: Pharmacists of old served herbal tea for toothache.
explanation.definitionFit: Apothecaries were the historical dispensers of medicines, forerunners of today's pharmacists.

clue.text: Ambitious head of gerontology supports drug

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: aspirin is a common painkilling drug

indicators.note: only the opening letter of gerontology is used

explanation.surface: An ambitious leader of elderly care backs a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspiring describes someone hoping and striving to achieve something, which is being ambitious.

clue.text: Confine to bed in A&E? That's novel!

indicators.note: the confining and bed words are placed inside the letters of the hospital department

parts.note: the letters A and E, as in accident and emergency
to dam water is to hold it back or confine it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient is kept bedbound in casualty, which is something new.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is a British hospital's accident and emergency department; its two letters go round DAMBED. 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is the 1859 first novel by George Eliot.

clue.text: Helping naughty ladies? That's explained away

parts.note: a helping is a portion, as is a ration

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone justifies serving food to misbehaving women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' makes ALISED from LADIES; 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rationalised has been given a plausible justification, so its awkwardness is excused.

clue.text: Contrived to get engineer into car

indicators.note: the engineer is placed inside the car

parts.note: Ford is a make of car
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: Someone schemes to get a mechanic into their vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Forced humour or a forced smile is artificial, which is what contrived means.

clue.text: Gesture is out of the ordinary

definitions.meaning: a movement made to convey a message, such as a wave

explanation.surface: A gesture is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a sign made to communicate; as an adjective it means striking or exceptional.

clue.text: Be sick after losing head and miss out

indicators.note: the word for being sick drops its opening letter

parts.note: to vomit is to be sick

explanation.surface: Someone feels ill after a knock and leaves something out.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out or skip it.

clue.text: Equestrian qualification

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a statement or contract that limits it

explanation.surface: A horseman's credentials.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseback rider is an equestrian, and a rider attached to a document qualifies it.

clue.text: Settled business

definitions.meaning: fixed and unchanging, as in a decision that is final

explanation.surface: A company that is established.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means fixed or settled; as a noun it is a business company.

clue.text: Rob finds Oscar in crowd

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for crowd

parts.note: a lot is a group of people, as in that lot
Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: A man called Rob spots someone named Oscar among a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' looks like a name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To loot is to plunder or steal goods, as rioters do, so it means rob.

clue.text: Fruit and veg. recipe

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, seen on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A recipe uses fruit and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear is a sweet orchard fruit related to the apple.

clue.text: Prisoner came across puzzle

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
to come across something is to find it

explanation.surface: A convict stumbled upon a brainteaser.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound someone is to baffle them, which is to puzzle them.

clue.text: Settle for last month's fish

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the last month of the year
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone accepts the fish from the end of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide a matter is to resolve it, which is to settle it.

clue.text: Laid out rightwinger for time- wasting

indicators.note: out means not in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, on the political right

explanation.surface: A Conservative was sacked for slacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory behaviour is slow and delaying, which wastes time.

clue.text: Bishop's shoddy accent

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rogue can mean defective or substandard, as in rogue goods

explanation.surface: A churchman speaks with a poor accent.
explanation.walkthrough: A brogue is also a sturdy shoe, which 'shoddy' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional accent, especially an Irish or Scottish one.
